key_insight: DiffHDR uses video diffusion models to plausibly reconstruct lost highlight and shadow detail from 8‑bit LDR videos, enabling realistic re‑exposure for HDR displays and post‑production. It treats re‑exposure as a generative restoration task conditioned on the input video and target exposure.
problem_solved: Recovers realistic HDR content from saturated and quantized 8‑bit LDR videos so luminance can be accurately remapped and re‑exposed for editing and HDR display.
method: Train a video diffusion model to generate missing high‑dynamic‑range detail conditioned on input LDR frames and desired re‑exposure parameters.
Enforce temporal coherence across frames (spatio‑temporal denoising) so results are stable for video playback and editing.
Leverage exposure conditioning and learned priors to hallucinate plausible shadow/highlight detail while respecting original scene structure.
impact: Enables filmmakers, editors, and vision systems to convert legacy LDR footage into usable HDR video for accurate display and creative re‑exposure; advances generative inverse‑imaging techniques for temporally consistent video restoration.
visual_elements: Before/after frame pair showing LDR input, reconstructed HDR result, and difference/highlight recovery overlay.

paper_title: DiffHDR: Re-Exposing LDR Videos with Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Zhengming Yu, Li Ma, Mingming He, Leo Isikdogan, Yuancheng Xu
